label: Multi-Target Codegen
summary: Current Kain can compile one .kn source into web, system, GPU, Unreal, and execution-lane targets.
recommended_kos_next_step: Stop treating Kain as a TS/SPIR-V-only lane and widen KOS-side build affordances to llvm, ue5, ue5editor, and hybrid packaging.
notes: KOS already shells out through the Kain CLI, but the current contract only modeled an older target subset.
This pass widens the contract surface so the newer targets can flow through manifests and Tauri calls.

label: Foreign Source Importers
summary: Upstream Kain actively supports C, Rust, TypeScript, and assembly import pipelines into Kain program form.
recommended_kos_next_step: Replace one-off importer assumptions in KOS with manifest-backed import jobs so C, Rust, TS, and crate ingestion use the modern Kain CLI surface.
notes: This is separate from host-backed runtime bridges.
The crate-ffi lane is modeled separately because it becomes a live runtime bridge after import.

label: Native UI Apps
summary: Kain can materialize desktop-native applications through the native-ui build lane instead of only emitting source text.
recommended_kos_next_step: Wire native-ui packaging into Zen/Tauri orchestration so authored world/native_ui roots can become first-class launchable tools from KOS.
notes: This is a packaged app lane, not a normal -t compile target.
It pairs naturally with world/native_ui roots and runtime bundle generation.

label: Viewport3D Runtime
summary: Upstream Kain now includes a real 3D runtime and viewport lane rather than just codegen stubs.
recommended_kos_next_step: Bridge Kain-authored viewport apps into the existing Zen/Tauri viewport shells instead of keeping the Kain 3D lane and KOS viewport lane conceptually separate.
notes: KOS already has strong viewport infrastructure, but it has not been modeled as a first-class Kain runtime app lane.
This pairs especially well with compiler-owned world projections.

label: Python Bridge
summary: Modern Kain includes an embedded Python runtime bridge for DCC- and tool-oriented workflows.
recommended_kos_next_step: Unify the existing KOS Python sidecar with the Kain runtime bridge contract instead of treating Python as a completely separate subsystem.
notes: KOS already exposes Python commands in Tauri, so this is a strong parity target rather than a greenfield feature.
This is one of the highest-value DCC integration lanes.

label: Node Bridge
summary: Kain can execute with a Node/JS host bridge for local JS helpers, packaging, and mixed-runtime flows.
recommended_kos_next_step: Add a Node-hosted Kain runtime lane for tool packaging, script adapters, and asset pipeline helper execution.
notes: This is different from emitting JS/TS as a compile artifact.
The bridge matters when Kain wants to call live JS runtime helpers.

label: Rust Crate FFI
summary: Kain can import and bind Rust crates as a live runtime bridge instead of only compiling Rust output text.
recommended_kos_next_step: Expose selected owner-crate APIs in KOS through a manifest-backed Rust-crate bridge instead of duplicating glue in every host surface.
notes: This is potentially the cleanest way to let Kain drive existing Rust-heavy owner crates in KOS.
Strong candidate for mesh ops, asset transforms, and simulation helpers.

label: C ABI Bridge
summary: Kain supports a host-backed C ABI lane for native/runtime interop and shared payload contracts.
recommended_kos_next_step: Adopt the C ABI bridge only when a native/runtime seam in KOS genuinely needs a stable binary contract; do not use it where Rust-crate FFI is sufficient.
notes: This is more useful for external/native interop than for purely internal KOS glue.
It becomes more relevant if KOS grows more mixed-language runtime boundaries.

label: GPU Runtime Executor
summary: Modern Kain has a runtime-facing GPU execution lane in addition to plain shader artifact generation.
recommended_kos_next_step: Evaluate where KOS should consume Kain GPU runtime payloads directly versus only treating Kain as a shader source generator.
notes: This is stronger than the older KOS assumption that Kain mainly emits SPIR-V blobs.
It is especially relevant for simulation, compute, and authored GPU workflows.

label: UE5 Codegen
summary: Upstream Kain now has a broad Unreal-facing stack spanning runtime, editor, shaders, materials, graphs, blueprints, and config-adjacent surfaces.
recommended_kos_next_step: Make Unreal a first-class Kain publish target in KOS instead of keeping UE integration implicit in docs and side workflows.
notes: This is one of the highest-value strategic parity gaps for KOS.
The backend is broader than just emitting USF shaders.

label: Omni Orchestration
summary: Kain Omni coordinates mixed-language pipelines across Kain, Rust, Python, Node, shader, and Unreal-oriented surfaces.
recommended_kos_next_step: Use the new capability registry to define where KOS should invoke omni as the orchestration layer instead of rebuilding every mixed-runtime lane manually.
notes: This is a major firepower jump over the older KOS-side Kain model.
It pairs well with KOS pipeline manifests and Fabric-style orchestration.

label: Selfhost Lane
summary: Kain now has an explicit selfhost lane for compiler evolution and deeper Rust/Kain crossover workflows.
recommended_kos_next_step: Treat selfhost as a compiler/toolchain lane, not a normal content pipeline lane, but keep it visible in KOS so compiler-oriented workflows are not buried.
notes: This is mainly relevant for language/toolchain work rather than end-user asset workflows.

label: Compiler-Owned Intents
summary: Kain now ships the compiler-owned intent quartet: patch, converge, world, and orchestrate.
recommended_kos_next_step: Model patch/converge/world/orchestrate in KOS-facing tooling and manifests so Kain-authored editor/runtime intent flows can stay structured instead of collapsing into opaque script blobs.
notes: patch and converge are the most immediately practical parts today.
world and orchestrate are useful but still earlier on the execution/integration side.
